previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, morbid obesity, and recent MSSA abscess was admitted after presenting with confusion, vomiting, and acute renal failure with a peak creatinine of 8.1. He was found to have pre-renal azotemia due to dehydration, likely exacerbated by a rapid prednisone taper and concurrent use of HCTZ, leading to relative adrenal insufficiency. His mental status improved with IV fluids and doubling of his prednisone dose. Renal function returned to baseline, and he was weaned off antibiotics after cultures showed no infection. CK elevation resolved with rehydration, and atorvastatin was held. He was discharged home with instructions to slowly taper steroids, monitor hydration, and follow up with his primary care and rheumatology providers.

## Complex fluid collection, possibly rheumatologic or 
musculoskeletal.  Also mild myositis.   He was admitted, and 
underwent evaluation by vascular, ID, orthopedics and 
rheumatology.  His leg pain and swelling worsened 
symptomatically and he underwent MRI which was negative for a 
discrete fluid collection, but showed fluid and mild muscle 
inflammation.  ESR lower than when initially had fluid 
collection, as is CRP.  Aldolase and CK normal.  MRI with fluid 
(which is recurrent) and mild muscle inflammation, which is not 
new.  He was treated symptomatically with pain control, and will 
follow up with rheumatology for further evaluation and 
recommendations. ID recommended no further antibiotic therapy 
unless clinically there are new signs of infection. With 
conservative management, the patient's leg became less 
erythematous and tender and showed signs of improvement. The 
patient's PCP is concerned about his worsening status since 
starting biologics for psoriatic arthritis and outpatient for 
consideration of further management of this medication will be 
by rheumatology.
